entries.test: Public service-level revenue and compute-cost figures would show whether every relevant AI service subsidizes compute and loses money because of that subsidy.
entries.note: The universal wording permits a profitable service to serve as a counterexample.

entries.test: Published subscription terms, customer representations, and service economics would show whether providers sold economically unsustainable subscriptions while misrepresenting their sustainability.
entries.note: The accusation contains an economic and commercial claim despite its loaded wording.

entries.test: Documented sustained profitability of an LLM service that does not charge each user's actual token consumption would falsify the economic impossibility claim.
entries.note: This combines a historical assertion with an unlimited future prediction and evaluative language.
'Closing time' does not identify a shared outcome such as bankruptcy, contraction, or the end of subscriptions.
The business-return assertion is explicitly uncertain. The separate universal assertion about studies could be checked if extracted independently.
Neither which businesses 'actually care' nor what constitutes substantial difficulty justifying costs has a shared test.
The forecast depends on investor scrutiny and explicitly says 'likely'.

entries.test: Public investor statements, fundraising reports, and spending restrictions around October 28, 2026 would show whether startups spending at least 10% of payroll-equivalent costs on AI tokens faced investor resistance to that spending.
entries.note: 'I think' introduces a firm 'will' prediction here. Its six-month horizon has arrived.

entries.test: Dated construction and operating reports, equipment inventories, and campus budget disclosures would establish Abilene's April 27 status and the support for the approximately $52.8 billion cost estimate.
entries.note: The normalization preserves the cost figure's status as an estimate.

entries.test: OpenAI's disclosed compute obligations, financing, revenue trajectory, and cash flows through 2030 would test whether paying those obligations requires the stated funding, growth, and cash-flow conditions.
entries.note: The normalization changes cash-flow positivity 'for any of these numbers to make sense' into an unconditional requirement. The stated annual growth and total growth also require separate arithmetic scrutiny.

entries.test: Oracle's available capital and disclosed remaining construction commitments would establish whether finishing the named project requires at least $150 billion more with partners contributing $30 billion.
entries.note: The source names Abilene despite surrounding discussion of the broader Stargate program; the normalization preserves that wording.

entries.test: Public Stargate financing agreements, customer contracts, and funding disclosures would establish whether projected campus cash flows exclusively fund the projects and OpenAI is their sole revenue route.
entries.note: This has a plain reading as a claim about existing financing and customer arrangements.

entries.test: Anthropic's compute agreements and annual spending commitments by the end of 2030 would show whether fulfilling its commitments requires agreeing to $25 billion to $100 billion in annual compute spending.
entries.note: This states a future requirement conditional on meeting its commitments.

entries.test: Public construction-capacity figures and financial models would test the approximately $156.8 billion annual revenue requirement using the stated PUE and revenue-per-megawatt assumptions.
entries.note: This is a present calculation under explicit assumptions; 2028 describes the capacity delivery schedule.

entries.test: AI data-center financial statements paired with utilization and tenancy figures would show whether operation below 100% necessarily produces multimillion-dollar losses and fails to cover depreciation.
entries.note: The passage asserts a general economic relationship rather than a particular future event.
'Tantamount to fraud' expresses an evaluative characterization without specifying a legal or factual fraud standard.
The extracted assertion concerns Anthropic's present private intention. Subsequent service removals would establish behavior, not necessarily that intention at publication.

entries.test: Public release statements, capacity records, and disclosed release-decision documents would show whether capacity constraints actually prevented Mythos's release and contradicted the stated capability rationale.
entries.note: The capacity explanation is a concrete factual allegation. 'Nothingburger' is an additional dismissive judgment.

entries.test: OpenAI's reported revenue growth and contractual payment schedules would show whether growth was slowing and whether meeting its obligations requires roughly tenfold business growth by 2030.
entries.note: The central claim concerns the current growth trajectory and financial requirements; the company-dying language is rhetorical framing.
The passage primarily judges AI's worth and its proponents' character; it supplies no shared standard for whether AI justifies its existence.
